additions.title: Tracking antibiotic resistance genes from vermicompost through the food chain: implications for soil-plant-animal health risk
additions.abstract: Despite the widespread use of vermicomposting in organic agriculture, the fate of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) along the soil plant animal continuum remains poorly understood. Here, we constructed a multi niche system spanning manure treatment (fresh manure, earthworm gut, vermicompost), environmental compartments (soil, rhizosphere, phyllosphere), and rabbit feces, and used metagenomic sequencing to track ARG transmission under vermicompost amendment versus unfertilized controls. Our results show that vermicompost reshapes the resistome in a niche specific manner rather than uniformly reducing ARG loads. The rhizosphere exhibited the greatest shifts in ARG diversity, abundance, and community structure, alongside more complex and interconnected ARG-mobile genetic element (MGE) co-occurrence networks. These effects attenuated progressively along the ecological chain, with the rabbit gut showing the weakest response. Nevertheless, several ARG carrying pathogens, particularly Escherichia coli, persisted across niches. MGEs were closely associated with ARGs, with clinically relevant ARGs physically co localized with insertion sequences, suggesting potential for horizontal transfer. Structural equation modeling indicated that vermicompost’s effects are largely indirect, mediated through microbial and MGE diversity. Overall, vermicomposting may inadvertently facilitate the spread of high risk ARG MGE combinations along food chains, underscoring the need for One Health oriented risk assessment that considers ARG mobility and host association.

additions.title: Universal machine learning potentials for two-dimensional materials mechanics and phonons
additions.abstract: Accurate modeling of phononic and mechanical properties in two-dimensional (2D) materials remains challenging because lattice vibrations are highly sensitive to computational details while mechanical deformation can involve complex nonlinear responses. Recent advances in universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) offer a promising route toward efficient atomistic simulations, but their reliability and application prospects across diverse 2D materials have not been systematically established. Herein, we perform extensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations and develop system-specific local machine learning interatomic potentials to establish a comprehensive benchmarking framework for evaluating the predictive performance of uMLIPs. Our results demonstrate that state-of-the-art uMLIPs, particularly the eSEN-30M-OAM model, can achieve remarkable accuracy and, in some cases, outperform customized passively-fitted local MLIPs trained for classes of materials. Although this level of accuracy is not universally guaranteed, these models reliably describe previously unseen 2D lattices, capturing key features of phonon dispersion relations and predicting complex mechanical responses across a diverse range of materials. Notably, for nanoporous and defective systems, where conventional DFT calculations become computationally expensive, uMLIPs retain high fidelity in describing both lattice dynamics and mechanical deformation. While challenges remain for large-scale finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations and higher-order property predictions, our systematic benchmarking identifies robust strategies that balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, this work highlights the strong potential of uMLIPs for predictive modeling and high-throughput screening of functional 2D materials, with promising extensions toward multilayer heterostructures, nanocomposites, and biologically integrated systems beyond the reach of conventional approaches.

additions.title: Deep-subwavelength Vibroacoustic Metamaterial Tactile Sensor: Modelling and Optimization
additions.abstract: Dynamic tactile sensing is limited by complex wiring, high fabrication costs, and poor scalability. This work focuses on the systematic design of a passive, wiring-minimal tactile sensing paradigm based on deep-subwavelength vibroacoustic metamaterial waveguides. Its development has been hindered by the lack of a tailored analytical model and quantitative performance metrics, preventing parametric analysis, comparative evaluation, and optimization. Here, we develop an analytical thermoviscous acoustic transfer-matrix model for this sensor class, reducing full-sensor simulation from hours of finite-element computation to tens of milliseconds. The model is validated against finite-element simulations and experimental measurements. We then introduce sensitivity and feature discrepancy as quantitative metrics, elucidate how design parameters govern performance, and construct an NSGA-II-based multi-objective optimization framework for automated identification of Pareto-optimal designs. Within the specified design space and evaluation conditions, optimized 2-, 3-, and 4-microphone configurations with 48, 144, and 288 sensing points achieve simulation-based Top-1 localization accuracies exceeding 95%, 98%, and 98%, respectively. These results are obtained from the validated analytical model and simulated datasets, not from physical prototypes. This work provides a quantitative design framework for this sensing paradigm, bridging the gap between proof-of-concept and systematic predictive design.

additions.title: State of the art in direct dark matter detectors: Technologies, performance, and future directions
additions.abstract: Identifying the particle nature of dark matter remains one of the most significant challenges in modern physics. Direct detection experiments aim to observe rare scattering events between dark matter particles and terrestrial targets, a task that demands extreme background suppression and sensitivity to minute energy depositions. This review critically assesses the current experimental landscape, organizing detector technologies by the fundamental physical trade-offs that define their scientific reach. We contrast the multi-tonne scalability of noble-liquid Time Projection Chambers (TPCs), which currently define the sensitivity frontier for high-mass Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), with the precision of cryogenic semiconductors and Charge-Coupled Device (CCD)- based sensors, which dominate the search for low-mass and sub-GeV candidates. Special emphasis is placed on the role of advanced reconstruction pipelines and machine learning (ML) as integral components of detector performance. Finally, we discuss the strategic roadmap for the next decade as experiments approach the neutrino fog, where coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEνNS) produces an increasingly significant and ultimately irreducible background that can mimic DM-induced nuclear recoils. We argue that future progress will rely not on a single technology but on a complementary global program combining increased target mass, ultra-low energy thresholds, improved background discrimination, and distinct observables - such as directionality and temporal signatures - to maintain robust discovery capability in the presence of neutrino-induced backgrounds.

additions.title: Beyond nuclear AR-V7: rethinking subcellular localization as a dynamic biomarker of endocrine resistance in mCRPC
Oncological and functional outcomes of focal irreversible electroporation for localised prostate cancer: a single institution series of 171 cases
additions.abstract: Focal irreversible electroporation (IRE) is an attractive choice for patients aiming to obtain local control of prostate cancer, while decreasing the postoperative risk of impotence and incontinence compared to whole-gland treatments. Retrospective review of a single centre prospective database of 171 consecutive primary IRE procedures for localised prostate cancer. Primary outcomes include oncological infield and out-of-field progression. Secondary objectives include post-IRE continence and impotence. The median follow-up is 35 months (3–90 months). The median diameter of the treated lesions is 11 mm (4–24 mm). Most patients had PI-RADS 4–5 abnormalities on prostate MRI, and 25 patients (15%) had ISUP grade 4–5 cancer. Of the 135 patients with >12 months follow-up, 84 had a surveillance biopsy of whom 8.3% had significant infield persistence, with significant out-of-field cancer in 14.3%. There was no difference in the risk of infield cancer persistence regardless of the pre-IRE ISUP score (p = 0.8), or tumour location (p > 0.9). The presence of low volume out-of-field cancer at diagnosis did not increase the risk of post-IRE cancer persistence/progression (p = 0.7). The prostate PSMA PET SUVmax of ≥10 did not increase the risk of infield or out-of-field recurrence of cancer (p = 0.3). A PSAD > 0.15 did not increase the risk of infield persistence or out-of-field progression of cancer (p = 0.8). Urinary continence was maintained in 167/171 (97.6%), while erectile function was maintained in 94/112 (84%) of sexually active patients who completed questionnaires. Of the patients who proceeded to post-IRE biopsy, 92% had infield ablation of clinically significant cancer with a low risk of urinary incontinence or impotence. Focal IRE of prostate cancer has promising short to medium-term outcomes and is associated with low risks of impotence and incontinence. Long-term follow-up of out-of-field progression risk is required.

additions.title: Prostate size and its effect on sexual function following convective water vapor thermal therapy
additions.abstract: Convective water vapor thermal therapy (CWVTT) effectively treats Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (LUTS) from Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH). While sexual outcomes have been studied across BPH procedures, the influence of prostate size on sexual function after CWVTT is unclear. We aimed to determine whether preservation of sexual function, measured by the Sexual Health Inventory for Men (SHIM), differs by prostate volume, particularly in larger glands. Following IRB approval, patients aged ≥18 undergoing CWVTT from October 2018 to August 2022 were identified by CPT codes 53,852 and 53,854. After applying inclusion/exclusion criteria, patients were stratified into prostate tertiles: small (≤38.5 cc), medium (38.5–55.6 cc), and large (>55.6 cc). SHIM scores were tracked longitudinally. Baseline demographics were similar across tertiles. Mean SHIM change from baseline to 3 months was −1.02, −2.10, and −0.46 for small, medium, and large prostates, respectively; only the medium group showing a statistically significant decline. Beyond 3 months, SHIM scores improved across all tertiles. Large prostates demonstrated a significant increase in SHIM over time (+0.18/month, p = 0.01) though significance was lost after adjusting for age, comorbidities, and baseline SHIM. Severe baseline erectile dysfunction (ED) predicted the greatest postoperative improvement, while men with no ED experienced mild decline. Age and baseline SHIM were the strongest predictors of outcomes. Men with larger prostates who undergoe CWVTT do not appear at increased risk of ED. In fact, the men with larger prostates have a faster recovery of sexual function than other prostate sizes. Patients with severe ED should be counseled on the potential for improvement in their sexual function following their procedure, especially 3 months onward with the exact mechanism being unknown. Finally, prostate volume likely plays a role in timing of recovery, although it is overshadowed by the influence of baseline SHIM scores and age.

additions.title: Correlation of intraprostatic lesional SUVmax during PSMA PET/CT and adverse pathology at radical prostatectomy
additions.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) is a novel staging modality for prostate cancer (PCa) patients with a high positive predictive value for lesions within and outside of the prostate. To assess the ability of the maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) at PSMA PET/CT to predict adverse pathology at radical prostatectomy (RP). Within a high-volume center database, we identified intermediate and high-risk PCa patients who had a PSMA PET/CT with an available intraprostatic SUVmax before RP between 2016 and 2021. Logistic regression modeling was used to test for the ability of SUVmax to predict non-organ confined disease or adverse pathology (non-organ confined and/or Gleason grade group ≥3) during RP. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to compare biochemical recurrence (BCR)-free survival after RP stratified according to SUVmax. Overall, 544 patients were identified. Of those, median lesional intraprostatic SUVmax was 9.5 at PSMA PET/CT. Median PSA was 8.1 ng/ml prior to RP. 50.7% vs. 49.3% had D’Amico intermediate and high-risk characteristics. Median follow-up was 24.6 months. BCR-free survival at 48 months after RP was 72.1% vs. 62.2% (p = 0.03) for patients with SUVmax <9.5 vs. SUVmax ≥9.5 at PSMA PET. In logistic regression models, SUVmax (continuously coded and stratified in <9.5 vs. ≥9.5) represented an independent predictor for non-organ confined disease and adverse pathology. SUVmax ≥9.5 at PSMA PET/CT is an independent predictor of adverse pathology at RP. Moreover, it is associated with worse BCR-free survival after RP.

additions.title: Correspondence: persistence, progression, and PSA: what exactly does DEAR-EXT compare? Yanping Zhu, Xiaohui Wang, Yang Zhang, Shuangwu Lv
Utilization patterns of second-generation androgen receptor pathway inhibitors as first-line therapy for prostate cancer in the United States
additions.abstract: Second-generation androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) have transformed treatment for patients with advanced prostate cancer. Despite overlapping indications and comparable efficacy among these ARPIs, their staggered market entry and differing toxicity profiles may influence real-world prescribing. We characterized temporal trends and utilization patterns of these agents as frontline treatment for advanced prostate cancer in the United States. Using the Merative MarketScan database, we identified patients with prostate cancer receiving enzalutamide, apalutamide, or darolutamide between 2012 and 2023. ARPI therapy was classified as first-line if initiated after ≥180 days of continuous enrollment. Annual proportions of first-line initiation and overall utilization of ARPIs were assessed descriptively. Comparisons by geographic status, urbanicity, insurance plan, and metastatic status were evaluated using chi-squared testing and multivariable modeling. Among 1.1 million individuals with prostate cancer, 3773 patients received ARPI therapy, of whom 1914 met criteria for first-line analysis. Use of first-line darolutamide steadily increased, rising to 42% in 2023 and surpassing enzalutamide. First-line ARPI selection did not differ significantly by region, urbanicity, insurance, or metastatic status. Overall ARPI utilization increased 21-fold over the study period, with enzalutamide remaining the most common agent. In 2023, a higher proportion of darolutamide fills occurred in metropolitan areas (p = 0.0008), and among metastatic patients (p = 0.0058). Darolutamide rapidly emerged as the most selected first-line ARPI by 2023, without consistently observed differences by patient demographics. However, continued dominance of enzalutamide for overall fills may highlight durability of legacy therapy, particularly among non-metropolitan and non-metastatic populations.

additions.title: Beyond the Scalpel: how the PROTEUS trial redefines the role of the radical prostatectomy
From fungus fighter to cancer slayer: itraconazole as a multifaceted candidate for drug-resistant prostate cancer
additions.abstract: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains a lethal disease state with limited durable responses to existing therapies, including taxane-based chemotherapy. Resistance mechanisms are multifactorial and incompletely addressed by current treatments. Drug repurposing offers an accelerated pathway for the development of novel therapeutic strategies in treatment-resistant disease. This review synthesizes preclinical mechanistic data and clinical experience with itraconazole (ITZ), a clinically approved triazole antifungal, across prostate cancer and other malignancies. We evaluate the signaling pathways targeted by ITZ, barriers to its clinical translation, and opportunities for biomarker-driven combination therapy. ITZ functions as a pleiotropic anticancer compound that modulates multiple pathways implicated in prostate cancer progression and therapeutic resistance, including Hedgehog/GLI, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling, as well as drug efflux transporters. Preclinical studies demonstrate that ITZ reverses ABCB1-mediated docetaxel resistance, suppresses Hedgehog/GLI1 signaling, and inhibits cancer cell proliferation and invasion. Despite compelling mechanistic rationale, clinical activity in mCRPC has been modest, with limited durable responses, underscoring a translational disconnect. Advancement of ITZ into clinical practice is constrained by pharmacokinetic challenges, dose-limiting toxicities, and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers to identify responsive patient subsets. Emerging evidence further suggests potential synergy with immune checkpoint inhibitors through tumor microenvironment modulation, though this remains unexplored in prostate cancer. ITZ represents a potential adjunctive strategy to standard therapies within rationally designed, biomarker-stratified combination regimens for mCRPC. Target populations include patients with PTEN-null tumors (elevated Hh/GLI and PI3K/AKT signaling), ABCB1-overexpressing tumors (taxane resistance), or those progressing after AR pathway inhibitor therapy. Clinical advancement will require pharmacological optimization, development and validation of patient stratification biomarkers (GLI1/PTCH1, PTEN status, ABCB1 expression), and integration with therapies targeting complementary resistance pathways.

additions.title: Clinical and genomic determinants of extraordinary response and resistance to androgen receptor pathway inhibitors in men with metastatic androgen pathway modulator sensitive (APMS) prostate cancer
additions.abstract: Identifying clinical and genomic predictors of response to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPI) for metastatic androgen pathway modulator sensitive (APMS) prostate cancer is essential for improving therapeutic decision-making. Divergent outcomes are observed in practice, with some achieving exceptional responses (ER) while others experience early resistance or non-response (NR), the biologic basis of which remains unclear. A retrospective review was conducted of patients with APMS prescribed ADT/ARPI from 2015–2024. ER and NR were defined by upper ( > 53.36 months) and lower ( < 10.41 months) quartiles of progression-free survival (PFS). Objectives were to associate baseline genomic and clinical factors with ER/NR status, PFS, overall survival (OS) and PSA kinetics.. Among 3363 prescribed ADT/ARPI, 224 were treated for APMS, with 154 (69%) undergoing temporal molecular testing. Alteration of ≥1 tumor suppressor gene with or without proliferative gene co-alteration was associated with NR while no single alteration predicted achieving ER. ECOG < 1, lack of pain, low-volume disease, higher hemoglobin and albumin, and normal alkaline phosphatase were associated with improved PFS, OS, and PSA nadir <0.2 ng/mL at 12 months. Alterations in TP53 (HR 1.60 [95%CI 1.02–2.50], p = 0.039; HR 1.91 [95%CI 1.05-3.49], p = 0.035) and MYC (HR 2.01 [95%CI 1.03-3.91], p = 0.040; HR 3.81 [95%CI 1.81-7.99], p < 0.001) were associated with inferior PFS and OS, while BRCA2 (HR 2.12 [95%CI 1.02–4.42], p = 0.045) additionally associated with PFS, and RAD21 (HR 2.55 [95%CI 1.13–5.77], p = 0.024) with OS. On multivariable analysis, MYC gain associated with OS (HR 4.41 [95%CI 1.24-15.7], p = 0.022). Pathway-level analysis showed proliferative gene alterations were associated with failure to achieve PSA nadir <0.2 ng/mL at 12 months (HR 0.49 [95%CI 0.24, 0.98], p = 0.047). In this real-world APMS cohort, we identified pre-treatment clinical and genomic predictors of patient benefits and long-term survival with ADT/ARPI therapy.

additions.title: Germline genetic risk and prostate cancer–specific mortality in a population-based incident cohort
additions.abstract: Multiple germline variants are associated with prostate cancer (PCa) susceptibility and aggressive features; however, their value for predicting prostate cancer–specific mortality (PCSM) at the time of diagnosis remains uncertain, particularly among men with clinically localized disease. We evaluated associations between germline risk factors and PCSM among 14,644 men with incident PCa in the UK Biobank. Associations between PCSM and reported germline risk factors, including 11 genes recommended by the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN), nine other candidate genes, two common variants [KLK3 (I179T) and HSD3B1 (1245 A > C)], and three polygenic risk scores (PRSs), were tested using Fine–Gray competing-risk models accounting for non–PCa mortality. During a median follow-up of 6.73 years after diagnosis, 1581 men (10.8%) died from PCa. PVs in three NCCN-recommended DNA damage–repair genes (BRCA2, MSH6, PALB2) were individually associated with increased PCSM and were defined as Tier-1. Aggregated PVs in seven additional NCCN-recommended DDR genes (Tier-2) and the KLK3 I179T variant were also independently associated with PCSM. In contrast, HOXB13, nine other candidate genes, HSD3B1, and all three PRSs were not associated with cumulative PCSM risk. Overall, 14.45% of men carried Tier-1 or Tier-2 PVs and/or KLK3 I179T and experienced significantly earlier PCa-specific mortality. Importantly, associations remained significant among men without metastatic disease at diagnosis. Reported inherited susceptibility to PCa does not uniformly confer risk of lethal progression. Germline PVs in NCCN-recommended DDR genes and the KLK3 I179T variant identify a subset of men at elevated risk of PCSM, including those with apparently localized disease. These findings support consideration of selected germline markers for prognostic risk stratification at diagnosis to inform individualized management decisions.

additions.title: Prognostic value of cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma of the prostate after radical prostatectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis using contemporary consensus recommendations
additions.abstract: Cribriform pattern (CP) and intraductal carcinoma of the prostate (IDC-P) are recognised as adverse histopathological markers. However, their precise prognostic weight in the post-radical prostatectomy (RP) setting remains poorly standardised. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify the association between CP/IDC-P and biochemical recurrence (BCR). A systematic search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted for studies published from 2016 onwards, coinciding with the 2016 WHO and subsequent ISUP consensus recommendations. The primary endpoint was BCR. Hazard ratios (HR) were synthesised using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation. Eight retrospective studies were eligible for quantitative synthesis. The cumulative prevalence of CP/IDC-P was 27%. On univariable analysis, CP/IDC-P was significantly associated with BCR (HR: 2.76; 95% CI: 2.23–3.41). This association remained robust in multivariable models adjusting for pathological stage and Grade Group (HR: 2.59; 95% CI: 1.44–4.67) and CAPRA-based preoperative frameworks (HR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.03–3.08). Isolated CP demonstrated a more stable prognostic signal (HR: 3.16) compared to IDC-P (HR: 4.24), the latter being characterised by wider prediction intervals. The main limitations include the retrospective nature of primary studies and the inherent risk of confounding. CP and IDC-P are potent, independent predictors of BCR following RP. These findings support the mandatory reporting of such architectures according to ISUP standards and their integration into contemporary post-surgical risk-stratification algorithms to optimise follow-up and adjuvant therapy selection.

additions.title: Long-term oncologic outcomes of patients with grade group 1 prostate cancer and pT3a disease on final pathology
additions.abstract: Grade Group 1 (GG1) prostate cancer is biologically indolent and typically managed with active surveillance (AS), yet pT3a pathology is occasionally identified at radical prostatectomy (RP). Its prognostic significance in GG1 disease remains incompletely defined. Retrospective cohort of 40 patients with GG1 and pT3a disease on RP (2000–2022), confirmed on central pathologic re-review. Four patients developed biochemical recurrence (BCR); the cumulative incidence of BCR was 3.2% at 5 years and 10.3% at 15 years. No patient developed metastatic disease or prostate cancer–specific mortality. GG1 pT3a prostate cancer demonstrates excellent long-term outcomes. Adverse histologic features, not pathological stage alone, drive clinically meaningful risk. Late, stable PSA detectability alone does not signify meaningful recurrence.

additions.title: Insights gained from single-cell transcriptomics on the cellular identity and plasticity of prostate epithelial cells
Antifibrotic therapy for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms secondary to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
additions.abstract: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms secondary to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (LUTS/BPH) are a ubiquitous condition estimated to affect over 50% of men over the age of 50 years. Various treatment options exist for men presenting with LUTS/BPH, including lifestyle and behavioral modification and medical or surgical treatment. Although multiple medical treatments exist, innovation for the medical treatment of BPH has not significantly progressed. A comprehensive narrative review was performed to evaluate prostate fibrosis as a contributor to LUTS/BPH and to identify potential antifibrotic therapies that may be applicable to the treatment of LUTS/BPH. A literature search was conducted in PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov for molecular, translational, and clinical studies relevant to fibrosis in benign prostatic diseases. Keyword searches included “benign prostatic hyperplasia”, “lower urinary tract symptoms”, “prostate fibrosis”, “fibrosis”, “antifibrotics”, as well as combinations of these terms. In this narrative review, we review the rationale and evidence for pursuing antifibrotic therapy as a novel treatment strategy for LUTS/BPH. We discuss potential antifibrotics that could be used for the treatment of LUTS/BPH. Finally, we discuss diagnostic studies that could be used in the future to identify patients with LUTS secondary to prostate fibrosis. Emerging evidence suggests that prostate fibrosis contributes to the development of LUTS. No antifibrotic therapies are currently being used, leaving LUTS secondary to fibrosis untreated. Antifibrotics are a novel medication class that could be used to treat patients who progress on current BPH medications.

additions.title: Salvage radiotherapy with or without hormonal therapy for biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
additions.abstract: Salvage radiotherapy (SRT) is the standard of care for patients with biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy (RP). Several randomized trials have evaluated the addition of hormonal therapy (HT), including androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs), to SRT; however, differences in patient selection, treatment duration, and endpoints have led to inconsistent results. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify the clinical benefit of adding HT to SRT in this setting. A comprehensive literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ASCO and ESMO meeting abstracts was conducted through April 2025. Randomized phase II-III trials enrolling patients with confirmed BCR after RP and comparing SRT with or without HT were included. Five trials (GETUG-AFU 16, RTOG 9601, RTOG 0534/SPPORT, RADICALS-HD, and SALV-ENZA), comprising 4536 patients, met the eligibility criteria. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for metastasis-free survival (MFS), progression-free survival (PFS), biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS), and overall survival (OS) were pooled using fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity. Analyses were stratified by HT duration (short-term vs. long-term), and subgroup analyses were performed based on pathological features. Short-term HT combined with SRT significantly improved bPFS (HR = 0.57; 95% CI: 0.46–0.71, p < 0.00001), PFS (HR = 0.58; 95% CI: 0.49–0.69; p < 0.00001), and MFS (HR = 0.82; 95% CI: 0.69–0.96; p = 0.02). Long-term HT was also associated with improved MFS (HR = 0.76; 95% CI: 0.61–0.94; p = 0.01). No statistically significant OS benefit was observed with either short-term or long-term HT. Subgroup analyses showed a significant MFS benefit in patients with positive surgical margins (HR = 0.68; 95% CI: 0.47–0.98; p = 0.04), whereas no clear benefit was detected in patients with Gleason score ≥8 or negative margins. The addition of HT to SRT improves disease control outcomes in patients with BCR after RP, particularly in those with positive surgical margins, although no overall survival benefit was demonstrated. These findings support a tailored approach to treatment intensification in the salvage setting.

additions.title: Persistence, progression, and PSA: what exactly does DEAR-EXT compare?
Exploring the utility of artificial intelligence in identifying progression of prostate cancer during active surveillance: A systematic review
additions.abstract: There is a recent surge in interest in the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in prostate cancer (PCa). When evaluating PSMA PET scans, AI has shown promise in detecting intraprostatic cancer and metastatic disease. This systematic review aims to assess the ability of AI to detect or predict the progression of PCa during AS. This systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (ID CRD42024529354) and conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed on Medline, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. Only studies evaluating AI in AS-eligible patients were included. After screening 842 articles, 12 studies were suitable for inclusion. The included studies comprised of 4622 AS patients of whom 1022 experienced progressions. Only three studies utilised developed their AI purely on clinicopathological variables. The area under curve (AUC) of these three AI ranged between 0.65 and 0.76, and the AI algorithm in one study outperformed traditional logistic regression. The integration of MRI parameters particularly the use of radiomics improves the ability of AI to predict progression as compared to clinicopathological variables alone. AI was also able to analyse serial MRI during AS and performs on par with the Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation (PRECISE) scoring system. The AUC of the AI algorithms which included MRI parameters ranged between 0.65 and 0.95. One of the limitations was the variability in study methodologies and inclusion criteria. The Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) was used and none of the studies had high risk of bias. AI shows promise in detecting PCa progression during AS. However, this systematic review highlights the need for larger prospective studies with external validation before AI can be integrated into the AS process.

additions.title: Clinical and surgical management of recto-urinary fistula after radical prostatectomy: a systematic review on current evidence
additions.abstract: Management of rectourinary fistula (RUF) is challenging due to limited data and variability in presentation and treatment. We conducted a systematic review of radical prostatectomy (RP)-related RUF to assess clinical features, diagnostics, treatments, and outcomes, and to propose a structured algorithm to guide management. We conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA guidelines to evaluate the clinical presentation, diagnostic strategies, management approaches, and outcomes of RUF following RP. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science was performed from database inception to January 2025. Data were extracted on patient demographics, symptoms, diagnostic modalities, management strategies, surgical repair techniques and treatment outcomes. A total of 455 cases of RUF following RP were identified across 34 studies. The reported incidence of RUF ranged from <0.01% to 1.5%. The most frequent presenting symptoms were urine leakage per rectum (60.7%), fecaluria (44.1%), and pneumaturia (50.0%). Fecal and/or urinary diversion was utilized in over 60% of cases, with a median stoma duration of 3 months and an indwelling urinary catheter duration of 1 month. Conservative management (observation, fluid replacement and antibiotic therapy) was attempted in a minority of patients and was generally associated with success rates below 50%. Surgical repair was performed in nearly all cases, with the transperineal and transsphincteric approaches being the most commonly employed techniques. The median time to fistula closure ranged from 0.5 to 30 months, with reported surgical success rates varying between 41% and 100%. We propose a management flowchart based on our clinical experience, outlining the diagnostic and therapeutic approach to rectal injury and RP-related RUF. RUF after RP remains a challenging complication, often requiring stepwise management. Conservative treatments rarely succeed, and surgery is often necessary. Our proposed algorithm aims to standardize the approach to RI and RUF, guiding treatment decisions and improving outcomes.

additions.title: Cytoplasmic versus nuclear localization of androgen receptor splice variant 7 as a predictor of benefit from androgen receptor pathway inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (PROPHECY trial)
additions.abstract: Androgen receptor splice variant-7 (AR-V7), a constitutively active truncated protein, is linked to hormone therapy resistance. Nuclear AR-V7 in CTCs correlates with poor response and shorter progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) treated with ARPIs. The predictive value of cytoplasmic AR-V7 localization remains unclear. This exploratory study evaluated whether an AR-V7-agnostic CTC scoring criterion, including cytoplasmic detection, better predicts ARPI in this mCRPC setting. Baseline blood from 107/118 pre-ARPI mCRPC patients in the PROPHECY trial (NCT02269982) was analyzed for nuclear and cytoplasmic AR-V7 using Epic’s CTC platform. Associations with confirmed PSA50 response, OS, and PFS with abiraterone or enzalutamide treatment were examined. Correlations between AR overexpression, AR-V7 localization, and AR-V7 mRNA levels were assessed. Proportional hazards models adjusted for Halabi risk score and CellSearch CTC count (>5) evaluated cytoplasmic AR-V7 prognostic significance. At baseline, 10% (11/107) had nuclear-localized AR-V7 and 14% (15/107) had cytoplasmic-only AR-V7, totaling 24% AR-V7-positive. All nuclear AR-V7 cases showed AR overexpression vs. 67% of cytoplasmic-only cases. PSA50 responses occurred in 0% nuclear, 13% cytoplasmic-only, and 30% AR-V7–negative patients. Cytoplasmic AR-V7+ patients had worse PFS and OS than AR-V7– patients, but similar PFS compared with nuclear AR-V7 + , despite numerically better PSA declines and OS. Cytoplasmic-only AR-V7 is more prevalent than nuclear AR-V7 in mCRPC and is associated with poor PFS and intermediate PSA and OS outcomes. Assessing both nuclear and cytoplasmic AR-V7 in CTCs may improve risk stratification before ARPI therapy. This study clarifies the clinical relevance of cytoplasmic AR-V7 in circulating tumor cells from men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. While nuclear-localized AR-V7 predicts extremely poor response, PFS, and overall survival with AR pathway inhibitors, cytoplasmic AR-V7 expands the definition of AR-V7-positive status and identifies patients with equally poor PFS and intermediate response and overall survival outcomes. Assessing both nuclear and cytoplasmic AR-V7 fractions may thus improve risk stratification heterogeneity and could better guide poor-risk ARPI treatment decisions by avoiding ineffective ARPI treatment, helping personalize therapy, and improving outcomes in men with mCRPC.

additions.title: Real-world analysis of androgen receptor inhibitors in US patients with nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: DEAR-EXT study
additions.abstract: The real-world retrospective DEAR study in patients with nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) demonstrated darolutamide was associated with lower risks of discontinuation and progression to metastatic castration-resistant disease vs enzalutamide and apalutamide. This analysis expands on DEAR, including additional patients and follow-up, comparing prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, metastasis-free survival (MFS), and overall survival (OS). DEAR-EXT was a chart review of electronic medical records from patients in US urology practices who initiated androgen receptor inhibitors (ARIs) for nmCRPC from August 2019–March 2023. Outcomes included time to initial drug discontinuation, time to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), PSA response, MFS, OS, and safety. Adjusted Cox proportional hazards models were used for the primary analysis and inverse probability of treatment weighting and other sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the impact of potential selection bias and confounding factors. Patients (N = 1375) received darolutamide (n = 565, 41%), enzalutamide (n = 609, 44%), or apalutamide (n = 201, 15%). Baseline characteristics were mainly similar across groups. Adjusted risk of discontinuation was significantly lower with darolutamide vs enzalutamide (hazard ratio [HR] 0.73, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61–0.88) and vs apalutamide (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.54–0.89). Adjusted risk of progression to mCRPC was lower with darolutamide vs enzalutamide (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50–0.80) and vs apalutamide (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.53–0.98). MFS was significantly longer for darolutamide vs enzalutamide (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.53–0.79) and vs apalutamide (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.93). The estimated MFS rates at 24/36 months were 72.3%/60.2% with darolutamide, 59.2%/48.3% with enzalutamide, and 63.9%/47.6% with apalutamide. Darolutamide appeared to be associated with higher PSA response, improved survival, and fewer adverse events vs other ARIs in a real-world setting. Results were consistent in a sensitivity analysis. Darolutamide demonstrated lower discontinuation rates, longer time to progression, and longer MFS vs other ARIs, highlighting its potential to enhance real-world patient outcomes. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06013475.

additions.title: Towards ecologically meaningful foundation models
additions.abstract: Ecology aims to explain and predict how organisms interact with each other and their environments across space and time. Yet both ecological data and theory are fragmented, leading to models that generalize poorly beyond specific systems or scales. Empirical evidence spans diverse modalities, resolutions and contexts, while theory is distributed across partially overlapping frameworks that are rarely integrated within a single predictive model. We argue that ecological foundation models (ecoFMs), trained on large, multi-modal ecological datasets and informed by ecological theory, offer a route towards unifying data and theory within a common framework. Beyond their scientific value for ecology, ecoFMs present a challenging and consequential testbed for machine learning, demanding advances in multi-modal representation learning, theory-guided modelling and uncertainty-aware inference. By learning shared representations of organisms, environments and interactions, ecoFMs could improve generalization, link pattern to process and enable synthesis across ecological subdisciplines. We outline a roadmap for developing ecoFMs, including requirements for data infrastructure, model architectures, evaluation strategies and governance, and assess where current machine learning and ecological approaches fall short. If developed responsibly and collaboratively with ecological practitioners and other actors, ecoFMs could enable new modes of analysis and strengthen ecological forecasting, while simultaneously driving advances in machine learning for multi-modal integration, theory-guided learning and generalization in complex, data-limited systems. Ecology struggles to make broad predictions, as ecological data and theories are scattered across many different sources, scales and approaches. Gardiner et al. propose to create ecological foundation models, which combine large, multi-modal ecological datasets with ecological theory, as a way to create more generalizable and predictive models.

additions.title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
additions.abstract: Fundamental limits to predictability are central to our understanding of many physical and computational systems. In deep learning, training outcomes are often difficult to predict and reproduce even when extrinsic sources of randomness are controlled, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here we propose riddled basin geometry as a unifying dynamical systems mechanism: every initialization leading to one solution lies arbitrarily close to initializations leading to different solutions, forming a fat fractal with structure at arbitrarily fine scales. Using a minimal neural network model, we analytically establish the classical route to riddling and derive a near-zero uncertainty exponent: even sharp increases in initialization precision yield only marginal gains in outcome predictability. In deep networks, intertwined training destinations and near-zero parameter-space exponents provide robust signatures consistent with riddling across the tested architectures, optimizers and training protocols, offering a common dynamical account of otherwise disparate empirical observations. We further introduce functional uncertainty exponents, extending these diagnostics of scale-insensitive irreproducibility from parameter space to the learned functions themselves. Together, our results support riddled basin geometry as a candidate organizing principle for irreproducibility in deep learning, with practical implications for optimization and the reliable deployment of artificial intelligence. Deep learning outcomes are hard to predict and reproduce. Ly and Gong propose fractal basin geometry as a mechanism: starting points leading to different outcomes interweave at arbitrarily fine scales, so greater precision yields little improvement.

additions.title: Microbial metabolism of methotrexate produces a STAT3 signaling molecule that alleviates gut inflammation
additions.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is a gold standard therapy for inflammatory diseases but has mixed therapeutic success in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The gut microbiota impact MTX efficacy and toxicity by metabolizing MTX and altering its bioavailability, yet how inflammation alters this metabolism, and how the resulting metabolites act on the host, remain poorly understood. Here, we find that gut microbes, notably Clostridium asparagiforme, metabolize MTX via carboxypeptidase G2 (CPDG2) to produce deoxyaminopteroic acid (DAMPA). In intestinal epithelial cells, DAMPA preserves mitochondrial health through mitochondrial signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling and enhances mitophagy. DAMPA administration attenuates intestinal inflammation in vivo, and remodels colonic mitochondrial pathways. IBD mouse models show reduced microbial CPDG2 and DAMPA, while patients with IBD show reduced CPDG2 gene abundance and suppressed DAMPA-enriched mitochondrial pathways, potentially explaining MTX outcomes in IBD. Together, these findings reframe microbial MTX metabolism from passive drug detoxification to active regulation of host mitochondrial and inflammatory homeostasis.

additions.title: The trans-acting potential of expanded repeat RNA
additions.abstract: In a subset of repeat expansion disorders, nuclear dysfunction extends beyond the originating locus through poorly understood mechanisms. Studies from the C9orf72 gene indicate that repeat RNAs interact with the genome in trans, suggesting that disease-specific repeat RNA sequences and structures may similarly contribute to pathogenic mechanisms in some of these disorders.

additions.title: Epidemiology of pediatric intensive care unit admissions and mortality in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
additions.abstract: Background Most childhood morbidity and mortality worldwide occur in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where critical care resources are often limited. While the pediatric critical illness etiology and mortality have been well described in high-income countries (HICs), comparable data from LMICs are fragmented. We aimed to characterize the causes of pediatric intensive care unit (ICU) admissions and deaths, mortality rates, and temporal trends in LMICs. Methods We systematically reviewed studies published from January 1, 2005-April 7, 2026 in English, Spanish, and French using PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Web of Science, and World Health Organization (WHO) Global Index Medicus. Eligible studies reported ICU mortality or causes of admission or death among children 1 month-18 years in LMICs. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed quality, and extracted data. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled ICU mortality, stratified by Global Burden of Disease Sociodemographic Index (SDI) and geographic region. Temporal trends in mortality were evaluated using meta-regression with the study mid-year as the moderator. This study is registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD42022317110). Findings Of 44,107 identified studies, 309 studies met inclusion criteria, representing 311,632 ICU admissions across 39 LMICs. The most common causes of admission were respiratory (19.7%), neurologic (5.6%), and shock (5.2%) conditions, with infectious etiologies driving the majority of critical illness across all organ systems. Pooled ICU mortality rate was highest in low-SDI countries (28.4%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 23.7-33.6%) and lowest in middle-SDI countries (10.0%, 95% CI 8.4-12.0%). There was a downward trend in mortality over time in low-middle and middle-SDI countries; with the trend in low-middle countries being statistically significant (p Interpretation Pediatric ICU mortality in LMICs remains substantially higher than that in HICs and varies markedly by socioeconomic context, with improvements in outcomes over time in low-middle and middle-SDI countries. The predominance of potentially preventable and treatable conditions highlights the urgent need to strengthen pediatric critical care systems, including early recognition, timely referral, and access to essential therapies, to improve child survival and global health equity. Funding None.

additions.title: Preeclampsia prevention by risk-stratified timed birth: a post-hoc Bayesian analysis of the PREVENT-PE randomised trial.
additions.abstract: Background PREVENT-PE showed that screening for preeclampsia risk at 35-36 weeks followed by risk-stratified timed birth reduced birth with preeclampsia overall. We aimed to assess possible benefit and harm within each risk stratum. Methods This post hoc Bayesian analysis included 4734 participants recruited at King's College Hospital, London, UK, in PREVENT-PE. The parent trial included women aged 16 years or older with a live singleton pregnancy, no major fetal abnormality or preeclampsia, and no conflicting trial participation. We included all 2871 intervention participants and 1863 control participants with stored serum and haemodynamic measurements that allowed retrospective calculation of 35-36-week preeclampsia risk. We estimated incidence proportions, ratios, and differences using independent Beta(1, 1) priors and binomial likelihoods. PREVENT-PE is registered with ISRCTN, ISRCTN41632964. Findings PREVENT-PE recruited between May 9, 2023, and June 7, 2024. Birth with preeclampsia occurred in 117/2871 (4.1%; 95% credible interval [CrI] 3.4-4.9) intervention participants and 106/1863 (5.7%; 4.7-6.8) controls; the posterior median incidence ratio was 0.72 (95% CrI 0.56-0.93), with probability of benefit 0.995. Estimates at 39 and 40 weeks favoured intervention and were more precise; estimates at 37 and 38 weeks were much less precise. Heterogeneity of treatment effect was not established. Overall incidence ratios were 1.03 (0.92-1.15) for emergency caesarean and 0.97 (0.76-1.25) for neonatal unit admission for at least 48 h. Interpretation The overall PREVENT-PE strategy is supported by randomised evidence, but these post hoc data do not establish different treatment effects across risk strata. The balance of benefit and harm of routine planned birth at 37-38 weeks remains uncertain and needs further evaluation. Funding Fetal Medicine Foundation.

additions.title: Syndrome-oriented CNS infectious complications after hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation and CAR T-cell therapy, part 1-viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis: recommendations from the Practice Harmonization & Guidelines Committee of the EBMT.
additions.abstract: Viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis are rare but life-threatening complications after autologous or allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HSCT) and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, associated with 30-60% mortality and frequent neurological sequelae. The absence of harmonised definitions and diagnostic criteria contributes to delayed diagnosis, underreporting, and substantial heterogeneity across centres. This EBMT Practice Harmonization and Guidelines Committee expert consensus provides practical recommendations for the definition, diagnosis, treatment, response assessment, and prevention of viral encephalitis/meningitis and viral myelitis, developed through systematic literature review and multidisciplinary expert consensus following EBMT methodology. We propose standardised diagnostic categories for proven and probable viral encephalitis/meningitis and myelitis, alongside a unified diagnostic algorithm integrating clinical assessment, neuroimaging, electroencephalography, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, and targeted virological testing. We highlight key neurotropic viruses for inclusion in initial cerebrospinal fluid multiplex PCR panels, including human herpesvirus 6, herpes simplex virus 1/2, varicella zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, adenovirus, polyomaviruses BK/JC, and selected community-acquired respiratory viruses, such as EV71, and recommend prompt, risk-based empirical antiviral therapy in suspected cases. These recommendations aim to standardise clinical practice, facilitate multicenter research, and improve outcomes. However, many rely on limited observational evidence or expert opinion, underscoring the need for prospective studies.

additions.title: Optimising cost and treatment simplicity of PD-1 blockade in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an economic analysis of three clinical trials in China.
additions.abstract: Background Economic burden of programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) blockade is a critical issue in locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC). Methods This pooled post-hoc analysis used individual-patient data from one phase II single-arm (NCT03984357 [recruitment: April 2020-October 2020]) and two phase III randomised (NCT03700476 [December 2018-March 2020]; NCT04907370 [August 2021-July 2022]) trials conducted in China, with Kaplan-Meier survival and Markov-model cost-effectiveness analyses. All patients aged 18-65 years with nonkeratinising NPC (8th TNM: T4N1M0 or T1-4N2-3M0) received intravenous PD-1 blockades: nivolumab (360 mg q3w pre-adjuvant/480 mg q4w post-adjuvant), sintilimab (200 mg q3w), or toripalimab (240 mg q3w). Regimens included 6 pre- and post-adjuvant cycles except toripalimab (11 post-adjuvant cycles). Temporal laboratory changes were analysed in patients with available data. Short- (≤4 cycles), intermediate- (5-9 cycles), and long-course (≥10 cycles) adjuvant PD-1 blockade strategies were compared in patients receiving ≥1 adjuvant cycle. Primary endpoint was failure-free survival; cutoff for follow-up: 20 March 2024, 19 February 2025, 21 March 2025, respectively. Findings Hypothyroidism-type disorder was associated with improved failure-free survival ( N = 673; p = 0.001). In 447 matched patients, longer adjuvant cycles versus the short-course conferred survival benefits in patients without concurrent cisplatin (intermediate-course: all p ≤ 0.012; long-course: all p ≤ 0.011), but not in those receiving it. Cost-effectiveness analysis favoured the intermediate-course. A 5- or 9-cycle adjuvant PD-1 blockade regimen was proposed for patients with or without concurrent cisplatin, respectively. The simplification delivered an average 36% reduction in per-patient costs. Interpretation In patients with LA-NPC, intermediate-course adjuvant PD-1 blockade had favourable overall performance in survival and cost-effectiveness. Prospective validation of these findings is warranted. Funding Noncommunicable Chronic Disease-National Science and Technology Major Project, National Natural Science Foundation of China, Tip-top Scientific and Technical Innovative Youth Talents of Guangdong Special Support Program, Cancer Innovative Research Program of Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Centre.

additions.title: Effect of a mHealth intervention on detectable HIV-1 viral load: a remote randomised controlled trial.
additions.abstract: Background Mobile health (mHealth) applications are needed for key populations of people with HIV who experience persistent difficulties with achieving and maintaining undetectable viral load (VL). Methods This remote randomised controlled trial (RCT) tested the efficacy of Supporting Treatment Adherence for Resilience and Thriving (START)-an mHealth application integrating self-monitoring of anti-retroviral therapy (ART) adherence with positive psychological skills (www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier NCT05140876). From 2022 to 2024, 286 sexual minority men with HIV residing in the continental United States who reported recent ART non-adherence and screened positive for a stimulant use disorder (i.e., 92% methamphetamine use disorder) were randomised (1:1) to START (n = 143) or a website control with referrals (n = 143). The primary outcome was detectable VL (>300 copies/mL) at six months (76% retention), measured via remote blood samples. Findings Participants randomised to START had 58% lower odds of detectable VL at six months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 0.42; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.19-0.93; p = 0.032). Among the 155 participants with undetectable VL at enrolment (54%), virologic rebound at six months was nearly two-fold greater in the website control versus START (48% versus 25%; p = 0.019). The number needed to treat was 4.75 (95% CI: 2.52-42.00) to prevent one instance of detectable VL. START effects on these VL outcomes were not maintained at 12 months. Interpretation A scalable, mHealth application significantly reduced odds of detectable VL in the short-term, primarily by preventing virologic rebound. Funding National Institute on Drug Abuse (R01-DA049843; UH3-DA058304).

additions.title: Syndrome-oriented CNS infectious complications after haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation and CAR T-cell therapy, part 2-focal brain infections and meningitis of bacterial, fungal, and parasitic origin: recommendations from the EBMT Practice and Harmonization Committee.
additions.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) infections in patients after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy are caused by a broad range of pathogens and associated with high morbidity and mortality. Lack of standardised definitions and uniform diagnostic approach contributes to underdiagnosis and heterogeneity in reporting. This EBMT Practice Harmonization and Guidelines Committee consensus document provides harmonised definition and recommendations on diagnostics, treatment, and response assessment for focal CNS infections and meningitis of bacterial, fungal and parasitic origin in cellular therapy recipients. Focal brain infections are predominantly caused by Aspergillus spp, Toxoplasma gondii , and Nocardia spp, whereas common bacteria are rare. Bacterial or fungal meningitis is rare and typically occurs late post-HSCT. Rapid diagnosis and treatment are crucial to improving outcomes. Benefits of corticosteroids in bacterial meningitis have not been evaluated in this population. Standardised definitions and outcome reporting should be adopted in registries and studies to improve comparability and strengthen the evidence base for management.

additions.title: Development and silent trial of DynaMELD, a Dynamic Model of End-Stage Liver Disease for personalized waitlist prioritization
additions.abstract: Background While the current prioritization system (MELD 3.0) improved waitlist mortality prediction, equity gaps persist, particularly for patients with cholestatic liver diseases whose clinical trajectories are poorly captured by static lab values. The sex disparity, while partially addressed, remains incompletely resolved. Methods We developed DynaMELD (Dynamic Model of End-Stage Liver Disease), a deep learning-based survival model capturing complex covariate interactions and leveraging the velocity of time-varying laboratory biomarkers to predict mortality or dropout risk. We trained DynaMELD on registry data from 53,046 ESLD patients on the U.S. liver transplant waitlist (waitlisted between January 1, 2016, and March 2, 2023) and externally validated it on 455 patients at University Health Network (UHN), Canada (waitlisted between January 1, 2016, and June 2, 2022). We integrated DynaMELD into the UHN's electronic health record system and conducted a retrospective silent trial on 382 patients waitlisted between June 3, 2022, and September 27, 2024, to simulate real-time model usage without influencing clinical decisions. Findings On a pre-COVID test split of the U.S. cohort, using 90-day pooled group concordance (PGCI) as a measure of fairness, DynaMELD achieved a PGCI 0.9% higher for female patients (0.848 vs. 0.841; p < 0.001), 8.2% higher for patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) (0.917 vs. 0.847; p < 0.001), and 9.6% higher for patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) (0.860 vs. 0.774; p < 0.001), compared to MELD 3.0. DynaMELD also achieved a 90-day concordance 0.6% higher than MELD 3.0 (0.827 vs. 0.822; p < 0.001). In the UHN silent trial, median estimated 30-day transplant probability across all patients was higher under DynaMELD than under MELD 3.0 (p < 0.01). Interpretation DynaMELD demonstrates that equity-driven model design and improved predictive accuracy are complementary objectives in transplant prioritization. Gains for historically underserved populations, together with feasibility of real-world deployment, offer a template for AI-powered equitable resource allocation in medicine. Funding Canadian Institutes for Health Research (CIHR) Project Grant (MB, RK); Data Science Institute at University of Toronto (RK); CIHR-Health Systems Impact Fellowship (MC); Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society Graduate Fellowship (MC).

additions.title: Smoking and dementia risk: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 61 prospective cohort studies and implications for tobacco control.
additions.abstract: Background Smoking has been identified as a modifiable dementia risk factor by three Lancet Commissions, yet dementia remains absent from most tobacco control strategies. The magnitude of the association across dementia subtypes, smoking categories, and population characteristics has not been comprehensively synthesised since 2015. Methods PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, and PsycINFO were searched from January 2013 to 31 August 2026, updating the 2015 review, which contributed 34 studies. Random-effects meta-analyses (Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment) estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses with tests for interaction and meta-regression examined effect modification by baseline age, ethnicity, follow-up duration, and adjustment for sex, education and Apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) genotype. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E). Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, I 2 and τ 2 and publication bias using funnel plots and Egger's test. Dose-response analysis of smoking and dementia risk was performed. Smoking population attributable fractions (PAF, unweighted and communality-weighted) for the risk of dementia were calculated. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD42025644539. Findings Sixty-one cohort studies (approximately 2.8 million participants) were included. Current smoking was associated with increased risk of all-cause dementia (RR 1.31 [95% CI 1.23-1.39]; number of studies (k) = 39), Alzheimer's disease (1.40 [1.08-1.80]; k = 15), and vascular dementia (1.52 [1.20-1.93]; k = 9). Former smoking was not associated with any outcome, and former smokers had a lower risk of all-cause dementia than current smokers (RR 0.81 [0.75-0.88]). I 2 ranged from 0% to 80%. Egger's test suggested small-study effects only for current smoking and all-cause dementia (P = 0.09). The communality-weighted PAF for smoking and dementia was 2.2% (95% CI 1.7-2.8). Dementia risk increased with smoking intensity as the pooled RR was 1.16 (95% CI 1.09-1.23) at 10 cigarettes per day and rose to 1.34 (95% CI 1.18-1.51) at 20 cigarettes per day. Interpretation Current smoking is consistently associated with higher risk of all dementia outcomes and increases with smoking intensity. Estimates refer to clinically diagnosed dementia syndromes [Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders/International Classification of Diseases (DSM/ICD)] and not to biologically defined disease. Although causality cannot be established from observational data, these findings support considering dementia and brain health outcomes in national tobacco control strategies and associated campaigns. Future work using objectively verified smoking histories is needed to clarify how age at cessation and time since quitting influence dementia risk and whether these effects interact with total years of active smoking. Funding None.
